The core REST API module is `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, which serves `/ws/rest/v1`. Four production methods there call `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet` directly, and one test does too. All of them are in the `openmrs1_12` resource package:

1. **`OrderSetResource1_12.save`** (lines 58–72) is the main one. It backs the `orderset` resource, so REST create and update requests go through it. It resolves member concepts and order types, then calls `saveOrderSet`.
2. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.save`** (lines 163–168) adds a member to its parent order set and saves the parent. It backs REST create for `orderSetMember`.
3. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.delete`** (lines 151–155) retires a member and saves the parent. It backs REST delete for `orderSetMember`.
4. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.purge`** (lines 171–175) removes a member and saves the parent. It backs REST purge for `orderSetMember`.

The only other caller is a test, `OrderSetMemberController1_12Test.shouldShowAllOrderSetMembersForAnOrderSet`. It would need review if the behaviour change alters what the save persists. I estimated its end line at 107 because I did not read past line 101.

The service declaration and implementation live in `openmrs-core`, not in the REST module. I listed them last because they are the source of the change rather than users of it.
